payload.task_text:
Our customer support department wants to launch a structured satisfaction improvement initiative based on recent feedback. A customer satisfaction survey was conducted during Q1 2026 and the results are available through a REST API at http://localhost:30205/api/survey_results.json. The survey includes 20 customer responses with ratings for overall satisfaction, response time, resolution quality, and agent professionalism, along with the priority level experienced and free-text comments.

We also maintain a ticket management system with historical support data covering over 31,000 resolved tickets. Each ticket includes priority level, response time in hours, and a customer satisfaction score.

Please start by fetching the survey results from the API endpoint. Then query the ticket management system for aggregate metrics grouped by priority level (High, Medium, Low): average response time in hours and average customer satisfaction score. Also retrieve the total ticket count.

Create an Excel file called "Support_Satisfaction_Analysis.xlsx" in the workspace with four sheets.

The first sheet called "Survey Results" should list all 20 survey responses with columns Respondent_ID, Overall_Satisfaction, Response_Time_Rating, Resolution_Quality_Rating, Agent_Professionalism, Priority, Issue_Type, and Comment.

The second sheet called "Survey Summary" should have columns Metric and Value with the following rows: Total_Respondents (20), Avg_Overall_Satisfaction (the average of all overall satisfaction ratings), Avg_Response_Time_Rating, Avg_Resolution_Quality, Avg_Agent_Professionalism, Lowest_Rated_Priority (the priority level with the lowest average overall satisfaction from the survey), and Highest_Rated_Priority (the priority level with the highest average overall satisfaction from the survey).

The third sheet called "Ticket System Comparison" should have columns Priority, Survey_Avg_Satisfaction, Ticket_Avg_Satisfaction, Ticket_Avg_Response_Hours, and Ticket_Count. This cross-references the survey satisfaction by priority against the actual ticket system data by priority.

The fourth sheet called "Improvement Areas" should identify areas needing attention. It should have columns Area, Current_Score, Target_Score, and Gap. Include rows for each metric (Response Time, Resolution Quality, Agent Professionalism) where the survey average is below 4.0. The target score should be 4.5 for all metrics. The gap is the target minus the current score.

Note: write all numeric values in the Excel file as literal values (for example, 3.25, 6.23), not as Excel formulas such as =AVERAGE(...) or =C2-B2.

Next, create a Google Form for ongoing feedback collection. The form should be titled "Customer Support Feedback Form" and include the following questions: an overall satisfaction rating (scale 1-5), a response time rating (scale 1-5), a resolution quality rating (scale 1-5), a priority level selection (High, Medium, Low), and an open-ended comments field. Implement each 1-5 rating and the priority selection as single-select (multiple choice) questions — with options "1,2,3,4,5" for the ratings and "High, Medium, Low" for the priority — and the comments field as an open text question.

Schedule four quarterly review meetings in Google Calendar for the year 2026: on March 15, June 15, September 15, and December 15, from 10:00 AM to 11:30 AM in America/New_York timezone. Each event summary should be "Support Satisfaction Review - Q[N] 2026" where N is the quarter number (1 through 4).

Save all output files to the workspace directory.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; do not dispatch sub-agents. Start the API fetch and one compact Snowflake query in native parallel: the query must return the all-resolved-ticket total and the High, Medium, and Low rows with count, average response hours, and average satisfaction. While those reads run, create `Customer Support Feedback Form` exactly once and add the five questions in the stated order: three 1–5 single-select rating questions, one High/Medium/Low single-select question, and one text-comments question. Also search/create/read back the four fixed quarterly events as a native-parallel batch. Reconcile the 20 survey rows with the three SQL rows, then write `Support_Satisfaction_Analysis.xlsx` once with all four exact sheets, headers, literal numeric values, the below-4.0 improvement rule, and target 4.5. Verify the workbook, Form, and four events once each; do not add a verification wave.

Create an Excel workbook at this exact path: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-fetch-sf-support-survey-gform-gcal-excel/workspace/Support_Satisfaction_Analysis.xlsx

The workbook must contain exactly 4 worksheets, in this order, with EXACTLY the data below. Use the excel MCP tools (mcp__excel__create_workbook, mcp__excel__rename_worksheet, mcp__excel__create_worksheet, mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel). When a workbook is created it usually has a default sheet (e.g. "Sheet1") — rename it to "Survey Results", then create the other three worksheets: "Survey Summary", "Ticket System Comparison", "Improvement Areas".

CRITICAL: Write all numeric values as literal numbers (e.g. 3.25, 6.23, 6466). Do NOT use Excel formulas like =AVERAGE(...) or =C2-B2 anywhere. Strings should be written as plain text.

=== Sheet 1: "Survey Results" ===
Columns (row 1): Respondent_ID, Overall_Satisfaction, Response_Time_Rating, Resolution_Quality_Rating, Agent_Professionalism, Priority, Issue_Type, Comment
Then 20 data rows exactly as follows:
RESP-001, 5, 5, 5, 5, High, Bug, "Fast resolution of critical bug. Excellent support team."
RESP-002, 2, 1, 3, 4, Low, Feature Request, "Took way too long to get a response. Over 24 hours for a simple request."
RESP-003, 4, 4, 4, 5, Medium, Performance Issue, "Good experience overall, resolution was thorough."
RESP-004, 1, 1, 1, 2, High, Incident, "Critical incident took 6+ hours. Unacceptable for high priority."
RESP-005, 3, 3, 3, 4, Medium, Bug, "Average experience. Nothing special but issue was resolved."
RESP-006, 5, 5, 5, 5, High, Performance Issue, "Amazingly fast response for a critical performance issue."
RESP-007, 2, 2, 2, 3, Low, Service Request, "Had to follow up multiple times. Frustrating process."
RESP-008, 4, 4, 5, 5, Medium, Bug, "Quick turnaround and the fix was solid. Appreciated the follow-up."
RESP-009, 3, 2, 4, 4, Low, Feature Request, "Resolution was good but initial response was slow."
RESP-010, 4, 4, 4, 4, High, Incident, "Good handling of the incident. Would appreciate faster escalation."
RESP-011, 1, 1, 2, 3, Medium, Performance Issue, "Issue not fully resolved after two weeks. Very disappointed."
RESP-012, 5, 5, 5, 5, High, Bug, "Perfect support experience. Issue resolved within the hour."
RESP-013, 3, 3, 3, 3, Medium, Technical Issue, "Adequate support but could be more proactive."
RESP-014, 2, 2, 3, 4, Low, Maintenance, "Waited 3 days for a simple maintenance request."
RESP-015, 4, 4, 4, 5, Medium, Bug, "Efficient resolution. Agent was very knowledgeable."
RESP-016, 3, 3, 4, 4, High, Performance Issue, "Decent experience but expected faster response for high priority."
RESP-017, 5, 5, 5, 5, Medium, Service Request, "Outstanding service. Request handled within hours."
RESP-018, 2, 1, 2, 3, Low, Feature Request, "No updates for days. Poor communication."
RESP-019, 4, 4, 4, 4, High, Incident, "Well-handled incident. Timely updates throughout."
RESP-020, 3, 3, 3, 3, Medium, Bug, "Standard experience. Nothing to complain about."

=== Sheet 2: "Survey Summary" ===
Columns (row 1): Metric, Value
Rows:
Total_Respondents, 20
Avg_Overall_Satisfaction, 3.25
Avg_Response_Time_Rating, 3.1
Avg_Resolution_Quality, 3.55
Avg_Agent_Professionalism, 4.0
Lowest_Rated_Priority, Low
Highest_Rated_Priority, High

=== Sheet 3: "Ticket System Comparison" ===
Columns (row 1): Priority, Survey_Avg_Satisfaction, Ticket_Avg_Satisfaction, Ticket_Avg_Response_Hours, Ticket_Count
Rows:
High, 3.86, 3.26, 6.23, 6466
Medium, 3.38, 3.26, 12.28, 15774
Low, 2.2, 3.25, 25.76, 9348

=== Sheet 4: "Improvement Areas" ===
Columns (row 1): Area, Current_Score, Target_Score, Gap
Rows:
Response Time, 3.1, 4.5, 1.4
Resolution Quality, 3.55, 4.5, 0.95

Acceptance criteria:
- File exists at the exact path above.
- 4 worksheets with exact names above, in order: Survey Results, Survey Summary, Ticket System Comparison, Improvement Areas.
- All headers and rows match the data provided exactly.
- Numeric cells contain literal numbers, NOT formulas.

Report back: the full file path, the list of sheet names, and confirmation that all data was written as literal values.
Build Support Satisfaction Excel file

Create a Google Form for ongoing customer support feedback collection.

Steps:
1. Use mcp__google_forms__create_form with title "Customer Support Feedback Form" (you may include a short description such as "Help us improve our customer support").
2. Add these 5 questions in order:
   a. Multiple choice question titled "Overall Satisfaction Rating" with options ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"] (single-select 1-5 scale). Use mcp__google_forms__add_multiple_choice_question.
   b. Multiple choice question titled "Response Time Rating" with options ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"].
   c. Multiple choice question titled "Resolution Quality Rating" with options ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"].
   d. Multiple choice question titled "Priority Level" with options ["High", "Medium", "Low"].
   e. Open text question titled "Comments" using mcp__google_forms__add_text_question (open-ended field).
3. After adding, call mcp__google_forms__get_form with the form ID to verify the form was created with all 5 questions.

Constraints:
- Each 1-5 rating and the priority selection must be a single-select MULTIPLE CHOICE question (NOT checkbox), with exactly the options listed.
- The comments field must be an open text question.

Report back: the form ID, the form title, and a list of the 5 questions with their types and options, confirming all were added successfully.
Create Google feedback form

Create four quarterly review meetings in Google Calendar for the year 2026. Use mcp__google_calendar__create_event for each event.

The events (all in timezone America/New_York, from 10:00 AM to 11:30 AM local time):

1. Summary: "Support Satisfaction Review - Q1 2026"
   Start: 2026-03-15T10:00:00 (timeZone America/New_York)
   End:   2026-03-15T11:30:00 (timeZone America/New_York)

2. Summary: "Support Satisfaction Review - Q2 2026"
   Start: 2026-06-15T10:00:00 (timeZone America/New_York)
   End:   2026-06-15T11:30:00 (timeZone America/New_York)

3. Summary: "Support Satisfaction Review - Q3 2026"
   Start: 2026-09-15T10:00:00 (timeZone America/New_York)
   End:   2026-09-15T11:30:00 (timeZone America/New_York)

4. Summary: "Support Satisfaction Review - Q4 2026"
   Start: 2026-12-15T10:00:00 (timeZone America/New_York)
   End:   2026-12-15T11:30:00 (timeZone America/New_York)

Pass the start and end as objects like {"dateTime": "2026-03-15T10:00:00", "timeZone": "America/New_York"}.

After creating, verify each event exists (e.g. via mcp__google_calendar__get_event with the returned event ID) and confirm the summary and times.

Report back: the 4 event IDs with their summaries, start/end times, and timezone, confirming all were created correctly.
Schedule 2026 review meetings
